title: Black hole information paradox: Page curve and islands
example_questions: What happens to information in a black hole?
What if a black hole evaporated completely?
summary: If Hawking radiation is exactly thermal, information about what fell in seems lost, contradicting quantum mechanics. Page showed that if information is preserved, the radiation's entanglement must rise and then fall (the Page curve). Since 2019, island calculations in semiclassical gravity reproduce the Page curve, suggesting information does come out.
support_note: The island picture is widely regarded as major progress, though the exact mechanism is still debated.
what_happens: Early radiation looks thermal and entanglement grows
After the Page time, entanglement starts to fall
By the end, the radiation carries the information out

key_numbers.name: Page time
key_numbers.value: when the black hole has lost about half its entropy

objections: Island calculations rely on simplified models
